$note: NOVA MOTION model registry. Every profile was verified against upstream sources on 2026-10-29. status: recommended|supported|experimental|incompatible. The installer refuses 'incompatible' profiles with an honest explanation. Checksums are the Hugging Face LFS SHA256 values reported by the HF API for the exact pinned files.

models.name: AnimateDiff v2 Motion + Stable Diffusion 1.5 (fp16)
models.model_type: text-to-video (SD1.5 image UNet + temporal motion module)

custom_nodes.name: ComfyUI-AnimateDiff-Evolved
custom_nodes.note: Installed automatically by scripts/Install-Studio.ps1 into engine/ComfyUI/custom_nodes.

resolutions.note: Native generation size; safest VRAM usage.
~1.5x the pixels of wide_640 — may OOM on 4 GB VRAM even with --lowvram.

upscale_export_targets.note: Conventional resize, NOT AI super-resolution. Does not recreate detail.

models.memory_notes: Peak measured on comparable 4 GB Ada hardware with --lowvram: ~2.8-3.4 GB VRAM during 16-frame context sampling at 512x512/640x360. System RAM footprint ~4.5-5.5 GB while sampling (checkpoint + motion module resident). Close browser tabs before generating. VAEDecodeTiled keeps decode spikes small.
models.quality_notes: SD1.5-generation motion model: expect soft detail, occasional texture morphing, and dream-like motion at 64 frames. Trained sweetspot is 16 frames; longer clips use sliding-context fusion (uniform, overlap 4), which can drift in composition over 8 seconds. This is an honest limitation of the model, not of the pipeline.

models.name: AnimateDiff v3 Motion + Stable Diffusion 1.5 (fp16)
models.model_type: text-to-video (SD1.5 image UNet + v3 motion module)
models.memory_notes: Same envelope as the v2 profile. The v3 motion module needs its small adapter file; beta schedule is handled by 'autoselect'. For clips longer than 16 frames, v3 benefits from positional-encoding adjustment — NOVA MOTION uses the plain sliding-context route, so expect somewhat more motion drift on 8s clips than with v2.
models.quality_notes: v3 generally produces stronger motion than v2 at the 16-frame sweetspot; on long sliding-context clips the difference narrows and drift can be more visible without PE adjustment.

models.name: LTX-Video 0.9.8 (2B DiT, fp8)
models.incompatible_reason: The 2B DiT itself would fit in 4 GB VRAM quantized, but the required T5-v1.1-XXL text encoder is ~4.9 GB in fp8 (~9.5 GB in bf16). With only 8 GB of total system RAM (Windows alone uses 3-4 GB), loading the encoder plus the DiT exceeds the memory budget and will thrash or crash. We refuse to label this model 'supported' just because the files are downloadable.
models.memory_notes: Requires >=16 GB system RAM in practice on this class of GPU.

models.name: LTX-2 (19B audio-video DiT)
models.incompatible_reason: LTX-2 is a 19B-parameter model (LTX-2.3 is 22B). Even the smallest community GGUF quantization (Q2_K) is ~8 GB for the transformer alone, plus a multi-shard text encoder. Community reports of 'LTX-2 on 4 GB VRAM' were produced on laptops with 16-32 GB of system RAM, which absorb the block-swapped weights. With 8 GB total system RAM this machine cannot hold the model in memory at any quantization. Not installable here.
models.memory_notes: Q2_K DiT alone = 7.9-8.3 GB > total system RAM.

models.name: Wan 2.2 (1.3B/14B T2V)
models.incompatible_reason: The 14B variants are far beyond 4 GB VRAM / 8 GB RAM. The 1.3B 'TI2V' variant is borderline on VRAM with aggressive quantization but its upstream guidance targets >=12 GB VRAM / >=16 GB RAM for a usable experience, and 5-second 720p outputs still exceed this machine's RAM budget during VAE decode. Not offered as a supported profile.

models.name: HunyuanVideo (13B)
models.incompatible_reason: 13B transformer plus a multimodal LLM text encoder (~14 GB combined even quantized). Requires 24+ GB VRAM or 32+ GB RAM with heavy block swapping. Fundamentally out of scope for 4 GB VRAM / 8 GB RAM.
